title: Cap. IV Arg. 5: Eph. 1:5–6 — destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν; adoption only of the faithful
latin: Arg. 5. Quos Deus destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Jesum Christum, quosque in Christo tanquam dilecto acceptos, ii considerantur ut fideles: Sed omnes quos Deus elegit ad salutem, teste Eph. i. 5, 6, destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Christum, eosque in Christo tanquam in dilecto gratos facit: Ergo omnes quos elegit ad salutem consideravit ut fideles. Major ex eo probatur, quod nulla est adoptio in filios nisi per fidem, Joh. i. 12, Quotquot eum acceperunt; et Gal. iii. 26, Omnes enim filii estis Dei per fidem in Christo.
pass_a: Argument 5. Those whom God destined unto adoption through Jesus Christ, and whom he accepted in Christ as the beloved, those are considered as faithful: But all whom God elected to salvation, as Eph. 1:5, 6 witnesses, he destined unto adoption through Christ, and makes them acceptable in Christ as in the beloved: Therefore all whom he elected to salvation he considered as faithful. The Major is proved from this, that there is no adoption into sons except through faith, John 1:12, As many as received him; and Gal. 3:26, For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ.
pass_b: Arg. 5. Their syllogism: those destined unto adoption through Jesus Christ and accepted in Christ as the beloved count as faithful; but Eph. 1:5–6 shows that everyone God elects to salvation he so destines unto adoption through Christ and makes acceptable in the beloved; therefore everyone he elects he considered faithful. They prove the Major from John 1:12 and Gal. 3:26 — no adoption into sons except through faith; you are all sons of God through faith in Christ.

lemmas.gloss: adoption into sons only through faith

title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol: Major false — temporal adoption needs faith; eternal destinatio need not
latin: Sol. Major propositio falsa est. Nam quamvis perfecta adoptio temporalis involvat fidem, ut conditionem antecedentem, vel saltem in ipso momento adoptionis concurrentem; ac proinde nemo considerari possit ut actu adoptatus, qui non simul consideretur ut fidelis: tamen adoptio, vel destinatio εἰς υἱοθεσίαν in mente Divina ante jacta mundi fundamenta considerari et potest, et debet, absque consideratione fidei in nobis tanquam conditionis antecedaneae.
pass_a: Solution. The Major proposition is false. For although perfect temporal adoption involves faith, as an antecedent condition, or at least concurrent in the very moment of adoption; and therefore no one can be considered as actually adopted, who is not at the same time considered as faithful: yet adoption, or destination unto adoption, in the Divine mind before the foundations of the world were laid both can and ought to be considered, without consideration of faith in us as an antecedent condition.
pass_b: Sol. That Major fails. Yes, finished temporal adoption carries faith with it — beforehand as a condition, or at least together with adoption in the same moment — so you cannot treat someone as actually adopted without treating him as faithful. But destination unto adoption in God's mind before the world's foundations can and must be thought without treating our faith as an antecedent condition.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol: eternal destinatio κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν — not according to foresight of faith
latin: Nec facit quicquam ad confirmationem Majoris, quod nulla est adoptio in filios, nisi per fidem. Nam licet nulla sit adoptio nisi per fidem, est tamen aeterna destinatio certarum personarum εἰς υἱοθεσίαν, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph. i. 5. et non secundum praevisionem fidei nostrae.
pass_a: Nor does it avail anything for confirmation of the Major, that there is no adoption into sons, except through faith. For although there be no adoption except through faith, there is nonetheless an eternal destination of certain persons unto adoption, according to the good pleasure of his will, Eph. 1:5, and not according to the foresight of our faith.
pass_b: And it does the Major no good to say there is no sonship-adoption except through faith. Grant the point: there is still an eternal destination of certain persons unto adoption according to the good pleasure of his will (Eph. 1:5), not according to foresight of our faith.

lemmas.gloss: according to the good pleasure of his will
not according to foresight of faith

title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol close: faith is effect of εὐδοκία — Matt. 11:26; Augustine De praed. Sanct. 13, 19
latin: Nam fides credentium, qua distinguuntur a non credentibus, non consideratur ut antecedaneum hujus Divinae εὐδοκίας, sed effectum, Matth. xi. 26. Videndus est Augustinus De Praedestinatione Sanctorum cap. 13. et 19. Ubi accurate explicat haec ipsa verba Paulina quae urgentur a Remonstrantibus.
pass_a: For the faith of believers, by which they are distinguished from non-believers, is not considered as an antecedent of this Divine good pleasure, but an effect, Matt. 11:26. Augustine On the Predestination of the Saints chapters 13 and 19 is to be seen. Where he accurately explains these very Pauline words which are urged by the Remonstrants.
pass_b: Believers' faith — what sets them off from unbelievers — is not an antecedent of this divine good pleasure but its effect (Matt. 11:26). Augustine's De praedestinatione sanctorum 13 and 19 carefully opens these very Pauline words the Remonstrants press.

lemmas.gloss: faith as effect of good pleasure
